review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The load-bearing boundary-likelihood argument is invalid on the declared class because it treats π/(1−π) as harmless although opposite-overlap controls 1−π only near the arm's zero-propensity endpoint. Even at the mixed witness, the control arm has 1−π₀(x) asymptotic to x^{3/2}/2, so its asserted information norm is infinite for spline directions nonzero near zero, contradicting the finite-variance concentration and Hessian calculations used in the proof. The same defect occurs for both arms in the two-heavy construction and leaves the signed Riesz expansion, learned-propensity Gaussian law, joint QTE law, and subsampling coverage unproved. Consequently the TL;DR and project justification stale-overclaim uniform feasible transfer and inference; what remains established consists mainly of examples, score-law bookkeeping, and conditional algebra rather than the advertised limit theory. The absence of a valid central first-stage theorem also prevents a leading-journal paper score despite the extensive formal presentation.

HALTED AT TRIAGE: the math panel returned `revise` and its findings were never repaired, so this note is NOT established as mathematically sound — do not bank it as downgraded on this verdict alone. Open findings: dropped_weighted_variance@thm:gaussian-branch, undischarged_symmetric_leading_statistic@thm:vector-subsampling, related_work_incomplete@thm:joint-qte, unanchored_negative_positioning@thm:vector-subsampling
